title: The Asteroid Belt
objective: After this level you can describe the asteroid belt and why it never formed a planet.
summary: Between Mars and Jupiter lies a sparse belt of rocky and metallic leftovers that Jupiter’s gravity kept from forming a planet.

cards.headline: The asteroid belt isn’t like the movies. It’s mostly empty.
cards.body: Forget the movie scene where a ship dodges tumbling boulders. Spacecraft have flown straight through the belt without hitting anything. So what is it really, and why is it there?

cards.headline: The planet that never happened
cards.body: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. Most asteroids are rock; some are largely metal. It's building material that never got built. Blame the neighbor. Remember from Level 4 that Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined? Its strong gravity stirred up the material there and kept it from ever gathering into a planet. Hard to build a sandcastle while someone keeps kicking it.

cards.headline: Less than a Moon
cards.body: And there isn't much of it. All the asteroids in the main belt together have less mass than Earth's Moon. Spread that thin between Mars and Jupiter and you get mostly empty space. That's why spacecraft have crossed the belt without hitting anything. The movie version needs a lot more asteroids.

cards.fact: The biggest object in the asteroid belt is a dwarf planet.
cards.context: Its name is Ceres, and it's classified as a dwarf planet, in the same club as Pluto. So the belt's biggest resident isn't officially an asteroid at all. In a neighborhood of rubble, it's the one with a title.

cards.headline: Asteroid belt: crossed
learned: The main belt lies between Mars and Jupiter
Jupiter’s gravity kept it from forming a planet
All of it together weighs less than our Moon
Ceres, its largest object, is a dwarf planet

questions.prompt: Where is the main asteroid belt?
questions.explanation: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

questions.prompt: Why didn’t the asteroid belt form a planet?

options.label: It never had enough material to start
options.rationale: Gravity stirring is the main reason.

options.label: Jupiter’s gravity kept stirring it up
The Sun’s heat melted it apart
A planet formed and later exploded
options.rationale: There’s no evidence of an exploded planet.

questions.explanation: Jupiter’s powerful gravity stirred the material in the belt, keeping it from gathering into a single planet.

questions.prompt: From Level 4: Jupiter outweighs all the other planets combined. How does that connect to the asteroid belt?

options.label: Its huge gravity kept the belt’s material from forming a planet
Its mass pulled all the asteroids into its rings
options.rationale: Jupiter’s faint rings are dust, not asteroids.

options.label: It captured the belt’s missing planet as a moon
Its mass makes the belt spin faster than Mars
options.rationale: Its gravity’s effect was to stop a planet forming.

questions.explanation: Jupiter’s enormous mass means strong gravity, which stirred the belt and prevented a planet from forming there.
